SAM substrate states are stabilizer-class in the technical sense of Bravyi-Fattal-Gottesman (Ref. [81] of paper); the partition algebra ĥ^i·d̂^j acts as a closed group of discrete operations on integer occupation states. Consequence: paper Result 1 (Eq. 23) applies to SAM tripartitions.

C-12 has (u, d, e) = (Θ, Θ, m₃) = (18, 18, 6); u = d holds exactly. Under stabilizer-class state model with u-d symmetry, paper Result 2 gives G^(3)_2(C-12) = 0. Consistent with m(C-12) = 12 by definition; extends CR262 chain-step identification.

CR256's A-conjugate (sign flip on 1 ± p/R^(d+1)) is a reflected-construction operation on the partition algebra. By paper Result 4 (Eq. 40), this is equivalent to a dihedral-group permutation. Therefore A-operator's matter↔antimatter map IS the SAM analog of dihedral invariant D_{2n}.

R² = M + Θ = ℒ − Θ is structurally inclusion-exclusion on a tripartite system with two 81-element sides and an 18-element overlap. Under I1, paper Result 1 applies to this tripartition; the genuine multientropy at n=2 of this tripartition vanishes by Result 2.

CR262 carrier/container distinction maps to: containers (R, V, F) force destructive interference in reflected-construction permutations (paper Result 4); the resulting reflected entropy is incompatible with bound-state stability. Carriers (m₃, D², Θ, ĥV) admit stable GHZ-extractable structure.
